name: captcha
documentation: Server-side captcha verification behind one contract: Cloudflare Turnstile, Google reCAPTCHA (v2 and v3) and hCaptcha. Publishes the `captcha` route filter, taking the expected action as its argument ("filters": ["captcha:register"]) so a token minted for one widget cannot be spent on another route. Distinguishes a failed challenge from a spent token, a missing token, a wrong secret and a provider outage, because answering all five with one 403 either blocks real people or hides a deployment fault.
//default: CAPTCHA_PROVIDER defaults to 'disabled'. Installing the plugin without configuring it must not block every protected route — the first symptom would be a sign-up form nobody can submit. A disabled provider logs a warning once per process, because a filter that silently passes everything is worse than no filter.
//failclosed: CAPTCHA_FAIL_OPEN defaults to false, which is the OPPOSITE of the kernel's WafLayer and deliberate: the WAF inspects every request so failing closed takes the whole application down, while this guards a handful of named routes that carry the filter precisely because they are under attack. A misconfigured secret always blocks and is not covered by the flag.
